```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Root locator + dual-load idiom shared with the get-started vignette: the
# source tree (check and site-build contexts) loads through pkgload; a bare
# installed package (reader-side) loads through library().
.pkg_root <- function() {
  for (dd in c(".", "..", "../..")) {
    if (file.exists(file.path(dd, "DESCRIPTION")) &&
        file.exists(file.path(dd, "R", "treatment-report.R"))) return(normalizePath(dd))
  }
  NA_character_
}
PKG <- .pkg_root()
if (!is.na(PKG) && requireNamespace("pkgload", quietly = TRUE)) {
  suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(pkgload::load_all(PKG, quiet = TRUE,
                                                      export_all = TRUE)))
} else {
  library(msuiter)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`ms_extract()` discovers signatures **de novo** from a catalog. This guide
covers the K-selection evidence, the default consensus pipeline, and
swapping extraction engines through the registry. Building the catalog is
the subject of [Mutation catalogs](mutation-catalogs.html); using a known
reference instead is the subject of
[Fitting known signatures](signature-fitting.html).

## A catalog to work against

A small synthetic cohort seeded with three well-separated bundled COSMIC
signatures keeps the guide offline and fast:

```{r cohort}
ref <- ms_refdb_bundled()$SBS_GRCh38@matrices[[1]]
S   <- ref[, c(1, 5, 9)]
colnames(S) <- paste0("CS", 1:3)
E   <- matrix(rep(c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2), each = 24), 3, 24)
sim <- ms_simulate(S, exposures = E, burden = 4000, seed = 7)
sim
```

## K-selection evidence

`ms_select_k()` gathers two evidence layers over a rank grid: a
cross-validation reconstruction curve and a stability panel (multiple
replicates per rank, clustered and matched). The **arbitration rule** is a
hard gate: a rank is only selected if it passes the stability veto, and an
undecidable grid raises a structured error carrying the full evidence
table rather than silently picking a winner.

```{r select-k, error = TRUE, purl = FALSE}
err <- tryCatch(
  ms_select_k(sim, k_grid = 2:5, replicates = 4, max_iter = 80,
              seed = 1, k_folds = 3, n_seeds = 3),
  error = function(e) e)
class(err)[1]
```

The tiny synthetic grid above is undecidable — the veto rejects every rank,
and the error says exactly why each candidate failed. The evidence table
rides on the condition:

```{r evidence}
ev <- err$k_evidence
head(ev[, c("k", "cv_test_deviance", "avg_stability", "passes_veto",
            "veto_reason")])
```

This is deliberate: on a small or noisy cohort, K is genuinely undecidable
and the package refuses to pretend otherwise. In production analyses the
fix is exactly what the error message says — widen the rank grid, raise
the replicate count, and read
`plot_k_cv_curve()` / `plot_k_stability()` / `plot_reconstruction_panel()`
(see [The visualization gallery](visualization-gallery.html)).

## The default pipeline

`ms_extract()` with no `method` runs the consensus pipeline: an ensemble
of NMF replicates, Hungarian-matched consensus clustering, and a refit of
the consensus matrix. Pass the K you adjudicated (here the generative
truth, since the grid above was refused):

```{r pipeline, warning = FALSE}
ext <- ms_extract(sim, k = 3)
ext
```

The result is an `MsSignature` whose slots carry the extracted matrix, the
per-sample exposures, the pipeline stability evidence, and a summary of
the catalog it was extracted from (channel name and hash — the provenance
pin used by export and comparison):

```{r slots}
dim(ext@signatures)
head(ext@exposures[, 1L:4L])
ext@catalog_summary$channel_name
```

The `stability` slot is the consensus pipeline's self-report — read it
before trusting the ensemble: the average and per-signature stability of
the Hungarian-matched replicates, how many replicates ran, the consensus
restarts and rounds behind the clustering, and whether the consensus
converged:

```{r stability}
ext@stability$avg_stability
ext@stability$per_signature_stability
ext@stability$converged
```

The reconstruction quality of the extraction can be eyeballed against the
input catalog with `plot_catalog_profile()`
([the visualization gallery](visualization-gallery.html) shows it).

## Swapping engines

Extraction methods are engines registered in the package registry. The
default pipeline is consensus-based; a single-method extraction passes a
spec — for example the NMF engine with its update rule and iteration
budget:

```{r engine}
ext_nmf <- ms_extract(sim, k = 3, method = ms_nmf(engine = "kl",
                                                  max_iter = 80,
                                                  seed = 1))
dim(ext_nmf@signatures)
```

The registry also carries the ARD and sparse engines (`ms_ard()`,
`ms_sparse()`), and third-party packages can register their own — the
contract and the onboarding checklist live in the extending guide
([Extending msuiter](extending.html)). Because every engine speaks the
same `MsSignature` output contract, comparing engines is a one-line swap,
and the results can be compared against each other or against a reference
with `ms_compare()`
([Comparing signatures](comparing-signatures.html)).

One protocol note for that comparison call: of the three matching
protocols, `hungarian` and `islam` match on the signature matrices alone,
while `jiang` matches on sample-level activity and therefore needs both
exposure matrices — and only accepts them when the two catalogs are
cell-aligned (the same samples, the true dictionary fitted). For a
de-novo-versus-reference check like the one above, the signature-only
protocols are the ones that apply.
